what_happened: The agent told Sri that a rejection in the batch log was one of Athena's own requests. It was a different job: the shared build folder fix. That job was rejected for three reasons. It wrote test scripts the forbidden way, it skipped the slot clean-up, and it misread its request. The agent named the job from a log line without looking up its request. It had made the same mistake earlier the same day. No work was judged bad by this report. The report was wrong.
cause: Status is read from raw batch-log and queue lines that name a job only by id. Nothing ties a line to the job's request or its rejection reasons. The agent reports on a job without resolving what the line refers to, and Athena has no per-job status view that shows request, state and cause together. The agent's own promise to check is the only guard, and it already failed once today.
prevention: Add a per-job status command, such as `athena status <job>` or a batch summary. For each job it prints the id, the request title, the state (rejected, interrupted, running, landed) and the reasons (failed criteria, findings, checks). Batch log lines would carry the request title next to the id. Agent guidance would require quoting this output before saying anything about a job's state. That would have shown that the rejection was the build folder fix and why.
proposed_request: Add a per-job status view to Athena. `athena status [job-id]` should print, for one job or for every job in the current batch: the job id, the first line of its request, its state (queued, planning, running, interrupted, rejected, failed, landed), and the reasons for any rejection or failure. Reasons are the unmet acceptance criteria, the blocker and major findings, and the failed checks, listed separately. Also include the request title next to the job id in every drain and batch log line that names a job. Acceptance: (1) with a fixture batch of one rejected job, one interrupted job and one running job, the command prints the right state and request title for each, and the rejection reasons for the rejected job; (2) an unknown job id gives a clear error; (3) drain log lines that name a job include its request title; (4) a test covers the case where two jobs in the same batch are in different states, so a line cannot be matched to the wrong one.
